messages.subject: start values
parts:
When I was testing the goodness of fit for the model below I got the following error.

t0 = 4099359 54891.72 41439.77
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :
  initial value in 'vmmin' is not finite

I take it that I need to add start values to my model.
Would I have a start value for each variable? So 5 start values for this model?

For example  start=c(0,0,0,0,0)

Is the first start value related to riv in the model below?
How do I go about improving/changing the start value?

How do I know when I have the correct start value? The goodness of fit works?

Thanks for your help.

I


gdistsamp(lambdaformula = ~riv + lake + prec + ele + temp, phiformula = ~1,
    pformula = ~OBS, data = umf, keyfun = "exp", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", mixture = "NB")

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] start values
parts:
hi Ian,
 in your model there are 9 parameters in this order:  (intercept, riv, lake, prec, ele, temp, intercept, OBSSINGLE, dispersion).

 If the error is occurring from within the parboot function then it might be challenging to resolve this because parboot is simulating a large number of data sets and you won't be able to fix the starting values for the particular offending case.  I don't have any good ideas how to fix that.

regards
andy

messages.author: 403be63af7ebf220
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: start values
parts:
Hi Ian,

Dan makes a good point. I'd do that first. 

You should also try rerunning parboot a few times. Perhaps you were just unlucky and it simulated an extreme dataset. 

If neither of these options fix it, a crude workaround would be to do: 

parboot(..., report=1) 

then copy the reported fit-statistics that are spit out before it crashes. You could do this several times and then compare the simulated fit-stats with the observed fit stat (t0). 

Of course, if it crashes a lot, it's likely that the model doesn't fit well.

Richard
